preservedCurrentWork: The fresh adba Plugins destination argument, roster observation attachment, Plugins early return, and both Plugins call sites remain intact.
The original two Plugins pointer cases and Agent Network wheel-zoom case retain their assertions.
Default social friends remain empty outside the two opt-in Human scenarios.
The Human setup uses the third options argument to skip creating an unrelated Agent while preserving the original Agent Network default.
authoredChecks: Actual shipping Electron entry and renderer/preload are launched; Human message changes use the UI and real IPC, without synthetic renderer ports or seeded product storage.

The first actual Sign in saves a non-plaintext account-session record through the existing secret owner; subsequent lifetimes use the same directory and loopback issuer, cannot receive an inherited CI session file, and do not click Sign in again.
Runtime safeStorage availability and absence of simulated unavailable storage are asserted; only ciphertext file hash/bytes/key presence are recorded, not credential contents.
The controlled loopback service validates Human bearer/device binding, participant identity, send shape, nonempty nonce, bounded history limit, explicit afterId=0 and historyCursor/nextAfterId echo.
Idempotent external fixture state is keyed by clientRequestId and rejects content changes for a replay; it is not used to mutate the product's local message owner.

Readonly node:sqlite diagnostics inspect actual transcript_entries and hex-encoded metadata under the test-owned .conversations store; no INSERT/UPDATE, seeding, recovery repair, or cursor writes exist in the harness.
The offline case asserts a unique complete canonical row, timestamp, identity, physical sequence and local visibility during a real HTTP 503, followed by an actual new send after service recovery.

The held-receipt case observes a real pending/dispatching local row, closes the first actual process lifetime, requires restarted Host POST replay with the original nonce, and asserts one canonical SQLite/UI message.

The held-receipt case creates new draft B through the editor, closes/reopens another actual lifetime, attempts release on the original already-closed socket, and requires B's full persisted draft and UI to remain unchanged before a new successful send.
Process identity is collected from observed owned processes, with Linux executable symlinks read only for those PIDs; the actual utility service, Rust Coordinator and AppHost parentage are asserted.

Normal shutdown refreshes the still-owned process-tree union before closing, then requires every observed identity to exit before reopen. Cleanup SIGKILL is separately recorded and cannot turn a failed graceful shutdown into a passed assertion.

Initial process-table or first-window failures share windowless cleanup/output capture; later failures retain page/console/process/HTTP/database diagnostics, failure trace/screenshot and explicit video capture attempts.

Each actual Electron launch opts into recordVideo, each context starts/stops tracing, each milestone captures DOM/PNG, and missing video or cleanup errors fail the case rather than being silently accepted.
The two cases assert no unexpected HTTP request and no captured pageerror, use zero retries, and contain no skip/fixme/only.
The harness requires GitHub Actions and full target HEAD equality, records hashes of actual assembled JS/native inputs, and requires Node >=22.16 for the readonly SQLite API.

limitations: This is static review of authored tests, not evidence of any executed test, compiler success or product acceptance.
The original submitted A draft's retirement across a process restart remains explicitly unqualified; replacing it with a new B draft is not counted as proof of A retirement.
Late old-socket release is an observed release attempt after the old process and socket have ended, not a fabricated callback into the new renderer.
The shutdown scenario is graceful Electron close with observed descendant exit; it does not establish OS-kill/crash recovery.

The controlled service is not the deployed backend. Backend afterId=0 deployment, supported-platform packages, OS-keychain qualification, full visual/a11y/security/long-term stability and independent ACCEPT remain separate requirements.

Parent must build/stage the actual desktop JS entry, Rust Coordinator and AppHost from the tested exact H and inspect the resulting run artifacts. Input-file hashes alone are not proof that a build came from H.

For this source-assembled CI case, parent should keep FABUSHI_ELECTRON_EXECUTABLE unset (or separately bind any packaged executable to the exact candidate); the inherited harness supports that override for other tasks.
